nodes.text: Microarray Normalization Method Comparison (ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow). Bioc Workflow ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow analog: read raw microarray CEL/IDAT files, normalize with multiple methods (RMA, vsn, lumi, ComBat), compare normalization quality via PCA and variance estimation. For normalization quality comparison and method selection ONLY — NOT for differential expression statistical testing. For differential expression analysis from a normalized microarray count matrix, use nf-core/differentialabundance.

Germline variant calling and annotation from whole-exome sequencing (WES) data for rare disease workup — identify candidate pathogenic variants | germline short-variant calling from whole-exome sequencing reads (alignment, duplicate marking, base recalibration, HaplotypeCaller) → annotated VCF with variant consequences, frequencies, and clinical significance flags

RNA-seq analysis for rare disease workup — detect aberrant expression, splicing outliers, and allele-specific expression to support candidate variant pathogenicity | bulk RNA-seq alignment and quantification from paired-end FASTQ (STAR alignment, gene and transcript quantification) → expression matrix, splicing outlier detection, and allele-specific expression calls to support rare disease candidate prioritisation

Integrate WES variant calls and RNA-seq expression/splicing evidence for rare disease candidate gene prioritisation — cross-reference with HPO phenotypes, OMIM, and ClinVar | multi-omics integration of germline WES variants and RNA-seq expression/splicing outliers for rare disease diagnosis — combine variant pathogenicity, expression outliers, splicing defects, and allele-specific expression with HPO phenotype matching and OMIM/ClinVar lookups → ranked candidate gene list with evidence tiers

RNA-seq differential expression analysis to identify differentially expressed genes for downstream integration with epigenomic peaks | differential gene expression on bulk RNA-seq count matrix (DESeq2/edgeR negative-binomial model), two-group or multi-group comparison → per-gene log2 fold change and adjusted p-values

ATAC-seq open chromatin accessibility peak calling and differential accessibility analysis for integration with RNA-seq DE genes | open chromatin peak calling and differential accessibility on ATAC-seq FASTQ (alignment, MACS2 narrow peak calling, consensus peak set, accessibility quantification) → differential accessibility regions

ChIP-seq transcription factor binding peak calling to identify TF binding peaks for integration with ATAC-seq and RNA-seq | TF binding peak calling on ChIP-seq FASTQ (alignment, MACS2 peak calling with input control, consensus peak set, binding quantification) → differential TF binding regions

Integrate RNA-seq differential genes with ATAC-seq accessibility regions and ChIP-seq TF binding peaks — link peaks to genes via genomic proximity and/or correlation | multi-omics integration of transcript (differential genes) and epigenomic (ATAC-seq accessibility, ChIP-seq TF binding) layers — peak-to-gene linkage by genomic proximity and/or expression-accessibility correlation, identification of regulatory elements driving differential expression → integrated peak-to-gene regulatory map

Perturb-seq sgRNA guide assignment and cell barcode demultiplexing | demultiplexing and thresholding sgRNA capture reads to assign target CRISPR guides to individual cell barcodes from single-cell Perturb-seq data → single-cell guide assignment table and annotated AnnData/matrix

Perturb-seq hit calling and differential expression vs non-targeting controls | statistical hit calling and differential gene expression testing comparing perturbed cells against non-targeting control cells across each sgRNA target → significant perturbation hits and perturbation-induced expression profiles

Perturbation state representation and embedding using scVI and scANVI | deep generative modeling of single-cell perturbation transcriptomes using scVI unsupervised and scANVI semi-supervised conditioning on perturbation labels → joint latent space embedding and perturbation state representation

Guide assignment for Perturb-seq CRISPR screen: detect and assign sgRNA guide barcodes to individual cells from single-cell RNA-seq data, following the capture-sequence / guide-barcode demultiplexing approach described in Replogle et al. 2022 (Cell 185(14):2559-2575, DOI:10.1016/j.cell.2022.05.013) | sgRNA guide-to-cell assignment from Perturb-seq single-cell data — guide capture sequence detection, guide barcode demultiplexing, cell × guide assignment matrix → per-cell guide identity table

Hit calling for Perturb-seq CRISPR screen: identify genes whose perturbation produces significant transcriptional effects, comparing perturbed cells against non-targeting controls, following the differential expression / effect-size ranking approach from Replogle et al. 2022 | perturbation hit calling from Perturb-seq single-cell expression data — differential expression of perturbed vs non-targeting control cells, effect-size estimation and multiple-testing correction → ranked list of significant gene perturbations

Perturbation state embedding using scVI / scANVI: learn a latent representation of perturbed single-cell transcriptomes, annotating cells by perturbation identity, following the scVI/scANVI variational inference approach referenced in Replogle et al. 2022 | scVI/scANVI latent embedding of Perturb-seq single-cell transcriptomes — variational inference for dimensionality reduction, batch correction, and perturbation-annotated latent space → low-dimensional embeddings with perturbation labels

Perturb-seq guide assignment: assign gRNAs to individual cells from the CRISPR screen single-cell data (Replogle et al. 2022, Cell 185(14):2559-2575) | guide RNA assignment to cells in a Perturb-seq / CROP-seq single-cell CRISPR screen (gRNA UMI counts per cell barcode, thresholding/mixture-model assignment) → cell-by-guide assignment matrix with singlet/doublet calls

Perturb-seq hit calling: identify significant perturbation-induced gene expression changes from the guide-assigned cells | perturbation hit calling on guide-assigned single-cell CRISPR screen data — per-perturbation differential expression against non-targeting controls → significant guide/gene hits and affected transcripts

Perturbation state analysis: learn a latent embedding of perturbation-induced cellular states with scVI / scANVI | latent embedding of perturbation states from single-cell CRISPR screen expression data using scVI/scANVI variational autoencoders → perturbation state clusters, phenotypic map, and annotated cellular programs

IDAT → Normalisation → Differential Methylation → Gene Enrichment. EPIC/450K array methylation from IDAT — minfi load + functional normalisation, DSS differential methylation, missMethyl gene-set enrichment. Use when you want the DSS-based differential-methylation + enrichment wrapper chain. Also applicable to bismark bisulfite coverage from nf-core/methylseq.

Load IDAT files and perform functional normalisation using minfi for EPIC/450K methylation array data | methylation array IDAT loading and functional normalisation (minfi: read.metharray.exp + preprocessFunnorm) → normalised beta/M value matrix

Perform differential methylation analysis using DSS on the normalised methylation values | differential methylation analysis on a normalised beta/M value matrix (DSS: DMLtest for differentially methylated loci and regions) → per-CpG/DMR statistics with p-values and FDR

Perform gene-set enrichment analysis on differentially methylated results using missMethyl | gene-set enrichment on differentially methylated CpG/probe lists (missMethyl: gometh or gsameth accounting for probe bias and gene length) → enriched GO/pathway terms with adjusted p-values

Load EPIC/450K methylation array IDAT files and run functional normalisation with minfi | load raw Illumina EPIC/450K methylation array IDAT files and perform functional normalisation (minfi) → normalised beta-value matrix

Run DSS differential methylation on the normalised beta values | differential methylation analysis on a normalised methylation beta-value matrix (DSS) → differentially methylated positions/regions with statistics

Run missMethyl gene-set enrichment on the differential methylation results | gene-set enrichment on differentially methylated CpGs/genes with array-probe bias correction (missMethyl) → enriched GO/KEGG gene sets

Estimate human PK parameters from preclinical animal (rat, mouse, dog) data using allometric interspecies scaling | allometric scaling of PK parameters (clearance, volume of distribution, half-life) from preclinical animal species (rat, mouse, dog) to predict human PK parameters using power-law interspecies scaling → predicted human CL, Vd, t½ with R² quality metrics

Full mechanistic PBPK simulation with compartmental model and organ-specific clearance, with optional renal/hepatic impairment submodel for special population dosing | mechanistic PBPK simulation using a compartmental model with organ-specific clearance (hepatic extraction, renal filtration) incorporating predicted human PK parameters, with optional renal impairment (CKD stage-adjusted GFR) or hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh) submodel for special population dosing → plasma concentration-time profiles, AUC, Cmax, Tmax

Monte Carlo sampling across PK parameter distributions to characterize inter-individual variability in PBPK exposure metrics | Monte Carlo simulation sampling across PK parameter distributions (CL, Vd, ka variability) to characterize inter-individual variability in PBPK exposure metrics (AUC, Cmax) → population PK distribution, 5th/95th percentile exposure, variability statistics

PBPK Simulation — & Special Populations. Mechanistic PBPK simulation for predicting human pharmacokinetics from preclinical animal data. Step 1: to estimate human PK parameters from rat, mouse, or dog data. Step 2: full PBPK simulation with compartmental model and organ-specific clearance (optional renal/hepatic impairment submodel for special population dosing). Step 3: Monte Carlo sampling for variability characterization. Use for: species scaling, IND/NDA PBPK packages, first-in-human dose projection, and special population (renal/hepatic impairment) dose adjustments. Required for regulator

Run RNA-seq differential expression analysis to produce a ranked gene signature (e.g. treated vs control) | differential gene expression on bulk RNA-seq data (FASTQ or count matrix), two-group comparison → per-gene log2 fold change and adjusted p-values, producing a ranked gene signature for downstream connectivity analysis

Query LINCS/L1000 connectivity map with the RNA-seq gene signature to find drugs with matching transcriptional signatures | drug signature matching against LINCS L1000 / CMap perturbation database using a ranked gene signature from differential expression → ranked list of drugs/perturbagens with connectivity scores indicating transcriptional similarity

RNA-seq quantification and differential expression analysis to generate transcriptional signature | bulk RNA-seq quantification and differential expression analysis → ranked list of differentially expressed genes with log2 fold changes

Query LINCS L1000 / connectivity map databases to identify drugs matching the transcriptional signature | transcriptional signature connectivity analysis against perturbation databases (LINCS L1000 / CMAP) → ranked list of correlated or anti-correlated small molecule compounds

RNA-seq differential expression analysis to generate a transcriptional signature (up/down-regulated genes) between the user's conditions | bulk RNA-seq differential expression from raw reads (QC, alignment/quantification, count generation, DESeq2-style negative-binomial DE), two-group comparison → per-gene log2 fold change and adjusted p-values, ranked DE gene signature

Find drugs with matching (or reversing) transcriptional signatures by querying the DE signature against drug perturbation signature databases (LINCS L1000 connectivity mapping) | drug perturbation signature matching via LINCS L1000 connectivity mapping against a query DE gene signature → ranked compounds with connectivity scores indicating signature match or reversal

Phase A: Cardiovascular safety pharmacology simulation — in silico cardiac ion channel panel (hERG, Nav1.5, Cav1.2) inhibition, action potential duration, and QTc arrhythmia risk | in silico cardiac ion channel profiling and cellular electrophysiology modeling for cardiovascular safety pharmacology → ion channel IC50 estimates, action potential duration prolongation, and pro-arrhythmic risk scores

Phase B: Central nervous system (CNS) safety assessment — blood-brain barrier penetration modeling, neuroreceptor cross-reactivity panel, and neurobehavioral toxicity prediction | CNS liability assessment via QSAR-based BBB partition modeling and off-target neuroreceptor binding prediction → central nervous system toxicity profile and behavioral alteration risk indicators

Phase C: Respiratory safety profiling — in silico tidal volume, respiratory rate depression risk, and bronchomotor/plethysmography surrogate liability prediction | respiratory safety evaluation using target liability screening and ventilatory suppression modeling → predicted alterations in tidal volume and respiratory rate

Phase D: Integrated ICH S7A safety margin calculation and regulatory risk dossier synthesis — exposure-margin comparison against efficacious Cmax across vital organ systems | integrated safety pharmacology dossier generation comparing predicted vital organ toxicities against therapeutic exposure → safety margins (Cmax free / IC50) and regulatory risk synthesis report

ICH S7A Phase A — Cardiovascular safety pharmacology: hERG IKr channel blockade prediction, QT prolongation risk, and cardiac liability assessment for the input compound | ADMET cardiotoxicity prediction — hERG channel blockade (IC50), QT prolongation risk, and cardiac safety liability scoring from a small-molecule SMILES input → predicted hERG IC50, QT risk classification, and cardiac safety margin

ICH S7A Phase B — Central nervous system safety pharmacology: CNS liability prediction including sedation, convulsion, and motor coordination risk for the input compound | CNS safety pharmacology prediction — sedation risk, seizure/convulsion liability, motor impairment potential, and general CNS depressant/stimulant classification from a small-molecule SMILES input → CNS safety risk profile and functional observational battery surrogate endpoints

ICH S7A Phase C — Respiratory safety pharmacology: respiratory function risk prediction including airway resistance, respiratory rate depression, and pulmonary liability for the input compound | Respiratory safety pharmacology prediction — respiratory rate depression risk, airway resistance (bronchoconstriction) liability, and pulmonary function impairment potential from a small-molecule SMILES input → respiratory safety risk profile and predicted effects on respiratory parameters

ICH S7A Phase D — Integrated safety margin calculation and core battery compliance summary: combine cardiovascular, CNS, and respiratory risk profiles into an overall safety pharmacology risk assessment with safety margins relative to therapeutic exposure | Integration of three safety pharmacology risk profiles (cardiac, CNS, respiratory) into a unified ICH S7A core battery summary — safety margin calculation relative to therapeutic exposure, overall risk classification, and regulatory compliance checklist → integrated safety pharmacology report

Validate SMILES input file — one SMILES+ID per line, check parseability and canonicalization with RDKit | SMILES validation and canonicalization from a text file (one SMILES+ID per line) → validated, canonicalized SMILES list with IDs

RDKit RECAP decomposition of validated SMILES into scaffold + R-groups | RECAP retrosynthetic decomposition of validated SMILES into scaffold and R-group fragments using RDKit → fragment-scaffold mapping table

Run mmpdb to compute property deltas for fragment swaps from the RECAP decomposition | Matched Molecular Pair analysis using mmpdb — compute property deltas for fragment transformations/swaps from decomposed molecules → MMP database with transformation-property delta pairs

Rank novel scaffolds by frequency, drug-likeness, and SA score from the MMP analysis results | Scaffold ranking by frequency of occurrence, drug-likeness (Lipinski/Rule-of-5), and synthetic accessibility (SA) score → ranked scaffold table with scores
Validate SMILES input file (one SMILES and ID per line) | validation, parsing, and structure standardization of SMILES input files containing identifier and structure pairs
RDKit RECAP decomposition of molecules into scaffolds and R-groups | retrosynthetic chemical fragmentation using RDKit RECAP cleavage rules to decompose compounds into core scaffolds and R-groups

mmpdb matched molecular pair generation and property delta calculation for fragment swaps | matched molecular pair indexing and transformation mapping using mmpdb to compute property changes across structural fragment substitutions

Rank novel scaffolds by frequency, drug-likeness, and synthetic accessibility (SA) score | multiparameter scoring and ranking of generated molecular scaffolds based on occurrence frequency, drug-likeness metrics, and synthetic accessibility scores

Validate SMILES input file (one SMILES+ID per line) for the MMP pipeline | parse and validate a line-based SMILES+ID input file (syntax check via RDKit, deduplication, salt/invalid-entry filtering) → clean validated SMILES table with compound IDs

RDKit RECAP decomposition of validated SMILES into scaffolds + R-groups | RECAP retrosynthetic fragmentation of validated molecules (RDKit) → scaffold/core structures with attachment-point-annotated R-group fragments per compound

mmpdb matched molecular pair analysis: property deltas for fragment swaps | matched molecular pair indexing and transform extraction with mmpdb on fragmented compounds → MMP transforms with computed property deltas (e.g., logP, MW, activity) for each fragment swap

Rank novel scaffolds by frequency, drug-likeness, and SA score | scaffold prioritization from MMP results — rank novel scaffolds/cores by occurrence frequency, drug-likeness (QED/Lipinski-style rules), and synthetic accessibility (SA) score → ranked scaffold table

Validate expression matrix and clinical metadata for downstream limma-voom and GSVA/ssGSEA analysis | QC and validation of a pre-computed gene expression count matrix and associated clinical metadata — check matrix integrity, sample-metadata alignment, missing values, low-count filtering, and normalisation readiness → cleaned expression matrix and validated metadata table

Differential expression analysis using voom transformation, linear model with covariates, eBayes moderation, and topTable extraction (logFC, adj.P.Val) | limma-voom differential expression on a normalised count matrix — voom precision-weight transformation, linear model fitting with covariates, empirical Bayes moderation (eBayes), topTable extraction → per-gene log2 fold change and adjusted p-values

GSVA/ssGSEA gene set enrichment analysis on Hallmark MSigDB (50 gene sets), identifying top enriched pathways per group | GSVA/ssGSEA gene set variation analysis on a normalised expression matrix using the MSigDB Hallmark 50 gene set collection — compute per-sample enrichment scores, rank top enriched pathways per group → pathway-level enrichment matrix and ranked pathway list

Phase A — CNS safety pharmacology arm of the ICH S7A core battery: in silico prediction of CNS liabilities (functional observational battery / Irwin endpoints: convulsion risk, sedation, motor activity, coordination, reflexes, body temperature) for the user's compound | in silico CNS safety pharmacology profiling from molecular structure — predict CNS adverse-effect endpoints (seizure/convulsion risk, sedation, motor/coordination impairment, behavioral effects) → per-endpoint CNS safety predictions

Phase B — Cardiovascular safety pharmacology arm of the ICH S7A core battery: in silico prediction of cardiovascular liabilities (hERG/ion-channel inhibition, QT prolongation risk, blood pressure, heart rate, ECG effects) for the user's compound | in silico cardiovascular safety pharmacology profiling from molecular structure — predict hERG and cardiac ion-channel inhibition, QT/arrhythmia risk, blood-pressure and heart-rate effects → per-endpoint cardiovascular safety predictions

Phase C — Respiratory safety pharmacology arm of the ICH S7A core battery: in silico prediction of respiratory liabilities (respiratory rate, tidal volume, minute volume, oxygen saturation) for the user's compound | in silico respiratory safety pharmacology profiling from molecular structure — predict respiratory adverse-effect endpoints (respiratory rate depression/stimulation, tidal volume changes, pulmonary function liability) → per-endpoint respiratory safety predictions

Perform limma-voom transformation, linear modeling with covariates, eBayes moderation, and topTable extraction | differential gene expression testing using limma-voom transformation with covariate modeling and empirical Bayes moderation → log2FC, p-values, adjusted p-values

Compute GSVA or ssGSEA pathway scores across 50 MSigDB hallmark gene sets and identify top enriched pathways per group | single-sample gene set enrichment scoring using GSVA or ssGSEA on MSigDB hallmark gene sets across sample groups → pathway enrichment score matrix and group-level pathway comparisons

Validate expression matrix + clinical metadata (sample matching, missing values, distribution checks) | validation and QC of a bulk expression count matrix with matched clinical/sample metadata — sample-ID concordance, missing-value and distribution checks → validated matrix, validated metadata, QC report

limma-voom differential expression: voom transformation, linear model with covariates, eBayes, topTable (logFC, adj.P.Val) | differential gene expression on a bulk RNA-seq count matrix using limma-voom (voom precision weights, linear model with covariate adjustment, empirical Bayes moderation) → per-gene log2 fold change and adjusted p-values (topTable)

GSVA/ssGSEA gene signature scoring on MSigDB hallmark gene sets (50 sets); top enriched pathways per group | gene set enrichment scoring (GSVA and ssGSEA) of the 50 MSigDB hallmark gene sets on a normalized expression matrix → per-sample pathway enrichment scores and top enriched pathways per group
